## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: `Cache.set` stores keys without lower-casing them, while `get` always lower-cases, so any mixed-case key passed to `set` can never be read back. This review read both changed files in full (`app/cache.py` and `tests/test_cache.py`) and traced `set`/`get` through the new tests. The tests were read, not run. One verified strength: `test_entries_expire` patches `time.monotonic` on the module object that `app/cache.py` actually uses, so the expiry check is deterministic.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `Cache.set` method and raises `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds, updating the comment to match. It also adds tests for a set/get round trip, the default TTL value and entry expiry.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `c.set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `c.get("Alpha")` or `c.get("alpha")` returns `None`. `set` writes `self._store[key]` unchanged, but `get` (`app/cache.py:17`) always looks up `key.lower()`, which breaks the rule in `app/cache.py:14-15`: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first, or mixed-case callers create duplicate entries". `test_set_then_get_round_trip` only calls `set` with the already-lower-case `"alpha"`, so it passes despite the bug. — Any caller that sets a mixed-case key gets a silent cache miss on every read. Because `get` deletes only the lower-cased key, these entries also stay in `_store` forever and are never evicted. — Fix: Store under `key.lower()` in `set`, and add a test that calls `c.set("Alpha", 1)` and asserts that `c.get("alpha") == 1`.
